title: Philidor or something else? Choose a defence and say why
outcomes: Names what to check before choosing a defence: king in front of the pawn, rook on the sixth rank (counted from the attacker's side), pawn still short of the sixth
Predicts draw or win when only the defending rook's square differs
Applies the same three checks when the colours are reversed (Black attacks)

steps.text: In **Philidor: the passive defence that works** you set up the defence. In a game you must first *choose* it. Check three things, in this order: is my king in front of the pawn? Is my rook on the sixth rank, counted from the attacker's side? Has the pawn already reached the sixth? A rook placed elsewhere may lose; that is what the attacker wants in *Lucena: building the bridge*.

steps.caption: Black attacks with the e-pawn. White's rook holds the third rank, which is the sixth counted from Black's side. Draw (tablebase).

steps.text: **When the passive set-up works.** King in front of the pawn, rook on the sixth rank, pawn not yet on the sixth: the examples here are draws. **When it fails.** Put the defending rook far away, for example on the seventh rank on the other side of the board, and the same position can lose. Rule of thumb: keep the order from the first card and test each placement.

steps.title: Same position, the defending rook moves

steps.prompt: For each position you judged, which of the three checks (king, rook square, pawn rank) did you make first? Which one did you skip when you were wrong?
